blind_spot: PROOF_PHRASE regex specificity was not compared against wl_proofcheck.py validation constraints. Guard accepted low-information phrases like 'sampled N files' without required file names or counts.
Guard accepts long-form flags (--flag) but not short forms (-f). Static code analysis cannot detect missing coverage without explicit testing of all variants.
A one-time transient failure in CI leaves no code artifact to test. CI gates cannot distinguish environmental flakes from reproducible defects without reproduction or active root-cause hypothesis.
Missing verification that pytest file-change mode is 'strict:' not 'shared:'. Existing pytest gates check test pass/fail but not conftest.py tree-tripwire configuration itself.

No existing check reads ci_diagnose's runtime categorizations to verify they match expected classes for known run-cancel failure modes (watchdog-cancel, runner-lost, etc.). The tool is used diagnostically but not validated by assertions.

Existing checks validated plan references at the source level and checked consistency, but did not verify that a plan referenced in the post-push Plan line actually existed in the specific branch being pushed.

The stop hook's ci-red check reported a job failure from an older re-run attempt instead of the latest one. The check did not verify it was reading the LATEST attempt's result when multiple attempts existed for the same job.
Existing checks may verify ci-trace execution but not that --wait correctly blocks until commit reaches remote (ls-remote poll) or exits 2 on head-lag timeout.
